content:
mina: heads-up — saw a big perf regression on /org/dashboard after the 2026-03-22 deploy, charts stutter and initial paint jumps from ~400ms -> ~1.6s. dashboard error rate up a bit. https://perf.redwood.local/dash/ORG123

kyle: repro for me too. filters + open time-range makes it worse. can you share the network + bundle delta?

sasha: linking trace: https://perf.redwood.local/traces/sha-abc123 — flame shows long parse/compile on vendor chunk right after bootstrap. stack points to `charts` import.

mina: curious — we didn't change chart code. only change in that deploy was the new telemetry client and a tiny ux tweak (panel headers).

alexa: telemetry shows bundle size jump at build 2026-03-22T03:14Z: +1.8MB gzip on main vendor. attribution: `echarts-extra` and `chart-plugins` new imports. percent of requests hitting canary 10% at the time 

devon: saw this locally with `NODE_ENV=production` — running `npx source-map-explorer build/static/js/*.js` shows new modules:
```
+ 1.2MB vendors~echarts-extra.js
+ 600KB chart-plugins.js
```
likely a code-splitting regression pulled those into vendor instead of lazy chunk.

kyle: do we have a rollforward/rollback plan for the canary? last deploy note: `deploy-bot: canary 10% -> 2026-03-22T03:14 (sha abc123)`.

deploy-bot: Canary started for sha abc123 at 2026-03-22T03:14Z (who: @alexa)

sasha: would explain the 10% SLO bump. but why parse/compile spike for those users? maybe chunk order changed so large vendor is parsed on initial paint. check `prefetch`/`preload` flags in webpack config.

mina: grep'ed the PR that touched build config (PR #4321) — they added `import 'echarts/extra'` in chart-loader to enable a new gauge widget. it was supposed to be dynamic but the import landed top-level.

devon: ah. that's the cause. fix is to make it dynamic: `const extra = await import('echarts/extra')` inside useEffect or revert until we code-split proper.

alexa: ops suggestion: rollback canary to 0% while we patch. revert PR #4321 if quicker. I'm leaning revert since it's urgent.

kyle: agree. small revert PR and re-deploy. also add a build-time check to fail if any import increases main vendor > +200KB compared to baseline.

sasha: can we also add a runtime guard: only async import when the gauge is visible? defers parse.

mina: creating rollback PR and a follow-up ticket for stricter chunk budget checks (RN-3248).

devon: quick local patch: in chart-loader
```js
// before
import 'echarts/extra';
// after
export async function loadExtra() { return await import('echarts/extra'); }
```
will test and open PR.

alexa: also worth adding an alert in console SLO monitoring to flag initial-paint regressions > 2x baseline for canaries. if we had that earlier we would have caught it at 2% traffic.

kyle: assigning rollback to @devon, canary rollback plan: run revert PR -> deploy to canary 0% -> monitor 15m -> promote as usual. I'll own the rollout once PR is green.

mina: test steps for QA: 1) verify bundle sizes with `source-map-explorer`, 2) run `yarn start:prod` locally and assert initial paint < 600ms on sample org, 3) run canary for 10% for 15m. tagging @sasha for traces checks.

devon: opened PR #4330 (revert PR #4321) and added the async import + unit test. CI green. linking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4330

alexa: reverting canary now.

deploy-bot: Started revert deploy for sha def456 (revert PR #4330) at 2026-03-22T04:02Z by @alexa

mina: after revert, initial paint went back to ~430ms on canary samples. charts no longer freeze.

sasha: follow-ups: add chunk-budget CI gate, add canary alert rule, and audit other top-level imports in `ui/` for accidental sync imports. I'll own the audit.

kyle: adding a retro item: doc + checklist for UI PRs that touch third-party libs — confirm async or budget-approved.

mina: great — thanks everyone. I'll file the RN-3248 ticket with the steps and close this thread once the audit is in flight. :thumbsup:
